item.title: Everything is Brahman
item.description:
Everything is Brahman Shyam Subramanian

Source: TW

Author: Shyam Subramanian

Read Shyam’s blog ‘Self Knowledge’.
Read his other contributions at this site.

(Posted to the Advaitin Egroup, September 2006)

Everything we see/perceive IS Atman or Brahman. It already is Brahman as it is. In fact it alone IS.

The plurality we perceive, we experience, we objectify is not “hiding” or “covering” Brahman - it IS verily Brahman. This has to be very clearly understood.

item.title: Realization in the 'pot universe'
item.description:
A non-dual vision is self-realization : a pot analogy Dr. Shyam Subramanian

Source: TW

Author: Dr. Shyam Subramanian

Read Shyam’s blog ‘Self Knowledge’.
Read his other contributions at this site.

(Posted to the Advaitin Egroup, Feb ‘09; revised April ‘09)

There is a mistaken view held by many that with self-realization, the mind of an individual disappears and so does any perception of duality. This is in my opinion detrimental to a seeker, as there is a eternal wait for perceptual duality to end.

item.title: shravaNa, manana and nididhyAsana
item.description:
shravaNa, manana and nididhyAsana Dr. Shyam Subramanian

Source: TW

Author: Dr. Shyam Subramanian

Read Shyam’s blog ‘Self Knowledge’.
Read his other contributions at this site.

(Posted to the Advaitin Egroup, April ‘09)

shravaNa means hearing of course – but it is not simply a matter of the physical act of hearing. It is not meant that a mahAvAkya such as tat tvam asi is some sort of a Sanskritized ‘abracadabra’ where, as soon as those words are heard by a qualified seeker, the veils of ignorance will magically part and the Truth be revealed. ‘Hearing’ in this case means ‘understanding’.

item.title: The locus of avidyA
item.description:
The locus of avidyA Shyam Subramanian

Source: TW

Author: Dr. Shyam Subramanian

Read Shyam’s blog ‘Self Knowledge’.
Read his other contributions at this site.

(Posted to the Advaitin Egroup, April 2007)

I shall try to provide you my perspective based on a simple example. Take the case of a small old pot – let’s call it Mr. Pott.

Mr. Pott is in reality clay, the same clay that all other clay pots are. He takes himself to be only the pot. As long as he entertains a notion that he is a pot he is small, he has aged 20 years since he was born, lives in a poor home, has lost some of the colour on his head, etc.
